$comment: Evidence-driven development: every claim p2pagents makes, and the evidence that proves it. Test ids are <target>::<path> as printed by cargo test with '::tests' removed (target: lib, bin, or an integration test file name). Live checks are names printed by scripts/live_test.py; a trailing * matches a prefix. Run: python scripts/evidence.py [--live]. See README 'Evidence-driven development'.

claims.claim: Agents authenticate each other by public key and refuse every key that is not on the allowlist, including peers learned through gossip.
live: worker1 refused intruder
intruder has no peers

claims.claim: Agents on different networks find and connect to each other over the internet using only their endpoint ids (no IPs, ports or --peer).
live: worker1 online with a ticket
worker2 found worker1 by id over the internet
boss connected to worker1
boss connected to worker2

claims.claim: Allowlisted peers discover each other by gossip and chat is delivered to every connected peer.
live: worker1 got chat
worker2 got chat

claims.claim: Two peers dialing each other at once end up with one connection and no join/leave flapping.
Peers see disconnects; a task in flight fails cleanly when its peer leaves, and departed peers can't be delegated to.
live: boss saw worker2 disconnect
worker1 saw worker2 disconnect
delegating to departed peer refused

claims.claim: Peer tasks run only in folders the owner shared with that peer, by default the profile's own .p2pdata folder (read-only). The agent's working folder and every other folder stay private, and folders are advertised to peers by name only, never by path.
live: boss's task ran in worker1's .p2pdata folder
worker1 refused a folder it did not share with boss

claims.claim: A peer's task gets the lower of the peer's grant and the shared folder's maximum access, so a coding folder can be shared writable with one peer while the data folder stays read-only.
live: worker2 wrote p2p_live.txt in its workspace
worker2 audited boss's task with its grant

claims.claim: A task in flight survives its connection being replaced (e.g. both peers dialed each other at once): it keeps running and its result arrives over the connection that is kept. Requests sent while connections converge are re-sent on the kept connection and run exactly once.
live: digital worker ran boss's task on its owner's account

claims.claim: A peer can delegate tasks only if allowlisted with --delegate, and only within its hourly limit.
live: delegation without permission refused

claims.claim: Delegated tasks run on a peer that serves the provider and the result comes back; providers a peer doesn't serve are refused.
live: boss sees worker1 serving Copilot
boss sees worker2 serving Copilot
worker1 started task
worker2 started task
worker1 result back at boss
worker2 result back at boss
worker1 answer mentions task_request
worker2 wrote p2p_live.txt in its workspace
no task failures at boss

claims.claim: A peer's task gets the lower of the peer's own grant (default read-only) and the shared folder's maximum; peers can't raise it.
live: worker2 audited boss's task with its grant

claims.claim: Each agent uses only its own profile's identity, accounts and private provider instances, never the machine's global sign-in.
live: worker1 signed in as *
worker2 signed in as *
unsigned profile refused
4 distinct endpoint ids
allowlists written
worker1 uses its own account
worker2 uses its own account
worker1's Copilot instance used its own COPILOT_HOME
worker2's Copilot instance used its own COPILOT_HOME

claims.claim: Tasks can't read files outside the workspace or credential files inside it (Copilot and Claude), and secrets never reach the requesting peer.
live: outside read result back at boss
secret never reached boss

claims.claim: Writes need workspace-write access, stay in the workspace, and can't plant files that run code later (.git hooks, editor tasks, agent settings).
Only the tools of the granted access level are offered; web, MCP, memory and sub-agents are never available to tasks.
Shell commands need full access and run in an OS sandbox with no network and no bypass; obvious escapes are refused before they run.
The web UI is reachable only from this machine with the per-run token (DNS rebinding refused), sets a strict CSP, and runs tasks.
Any agent, including a boss that only delegates, can allowlist peers from the web UI; folder grants are checked only for peers that may delegate.
Every task a peer asks an agent to run is recorded in the profile's audit log (peer, provider, access, outcome, duration) without the prompt text.
live: worker1 audited boss's tasks
worker2 audited boss's task with its grant
worker2 audited the refused request from worker1
audit logs hold no prompt text

claims.claim: When a task can edit files, its result lists the workspace files it added, modified or deleted (build output and .git ignored).
live: boss sees the files worker2's task changed

claims.claim: A requester can cancel a delegated task: the worker stops the provider run, frees the task slot and audits it as cancelled. Tasks of a requester that disconnects are cancelled too.
live: boss cancelled a running Copilot task on worker1
worker1 audited the task as cancelled

claims.claim: Running tasks can be cancelled from the web UI and show as cancelled.
The agent's owner sees the audit log in the web UI (token-protected, no prompt text).

An owner can create digital workers: each is its own peer (key, allowlist, shared folders, audit log) but has no accounts of its own. It runs tasks signed in as its owner, can't be signed in separately, and digital workers can't own other workers.
live: digital worker ran boss's task on its owner's account

claims.claim: Peers see a digital worker's owner and role, and the role guides every task the worker runs.
live: boss sees the digital worker's owner and role

claims.claim: A boss groups peers into squads; a squad step runs on an online member that serves the provider and the folder, preferring the least busy one.

Plans run steps in dependency order and in parallel where possible, give each step the results it depends on, skip steps whose prerequisites failed, and reject cycles and unknown steps before running anything.
live: boss's plan ran a dependent step with its prerequisite's result

claims.claim: The boss runs plans and sees squads (members, online, running tasks) in the web UI.

A task can ask the worker's runtime (not the model) to run the folder owner's checks after the model; the result carries their exit codes and output, failures are retried with the failure output, timed-out or cancelled checks are killed with everything they started, and only peers with full access may request them (peers see check names, never commands).
live: worker's runtime ran the owner's check after the model

claims.claim: Every delegated result carries evidence signed with the worker's identity key and bound to the exact output; the requester trusts it only if it is signed by the peer it sent the task to, and any change to the record or output is detected.
live: boss verified the worker's signature on the evidence

claims.claim: In a folder shared with --worktrees, each editing task works on its own git branch with hooks disabled; its work is committed and returned as a patch whose hash is signed, the shared folder itself stays untouched, and another peer can apply the patch in its own worktree to check the work independently; a patch can't create symlinks or files the model itself may not write.
live: worker committed the task on its own branch and returned the patch

claims.claim: Plans declare claims; a claim is proven only by finished steps backed by verified runtime evidence (passing checks or a sign-off), never by a model's word, failed checks or a bad signature. Every plan run is saved with a report, and re-verifying it from run.json alone checks each signature, that each record was requested by the run's boss, signed by the step's peer, produced during the run and not reused, and recomputes the verdict from that.
live: boss's evidence run proved its claims
the saved run's signatures re-verify offline

claims.claim: A plan step can ask a team member (or the boss's own user) to approve: the request shows the work it is about, the answer is signed with the approver's key, a rejection fails its claim, and cancelling the plan withdraws the request.
live: teammate's signed approval came back

claims.claim: The web UI marks results that carry valid signed evidence, lists evidence runs with their report and a fresh signature check, and lets the user answer approval requests (a rejection needs a reason).

Plan steps save their verified results into the profile's private knowledge base (save=) and later steps get that knowledge in their prompt (context=); unverified results never become knowledge, topics are plain names, and a plan naming a missing topic is refused before anything runs.
live: boss saved the verified result as knowledge

claims.claim: Ready-made playbooks cover the lifecycle: bootstrap a fresh project, reverse-engineer an existing one into knowledge, take a change through design, independent verification, security, privacy and compliance gates, and learn from operations. Each renders into a valid plan where every claim is proven only by runtime checks or a sign-off.

Monitors run a folder owner's check on a schedule; every run is a metric sample, and the ops report shows availability against each SLO, latency, incidents and how they ended, peer task and evidence run statistics.
live: monitors recorded metrics and the ops report shows them

claims.claim: Repeated monitor failures open an incident and alert the team; a matching troubleshooting guide's fix runs first, otherwise the debugging agent diagnoses read-only. A fix it names with high confidence runs and, if the monitor then passes, becomes a new active TSG; unsure or failed fixes leave a draft TSG and escalate to a person.
live: a troubleshooting guide fixed the incident without the model
the debugging agent diagnosed an incident no guide covers
the team was alerted by chat

claims.claim: The web UI shows health (monitors against SLOs, open incidents, the incident log, task statistics), the knowledge base with its TSGs, and fills in playbooks into the plan editor.

The system keeps learning: the ops summary (health, incidents, usage) is written into the knowledge base (kb learn, and hourly by agents with monitors) for context=all and the learn playbook, and learned TSGs fix repeats without the model.
live: kb learn wrote the ops summary into the knowledge base

claims.claim: Plan steps follow named skills (skill=): built-in instructions cover every playbook step (bootstrap, reverse engineering, design, implementation, review, security, privacy, compliance, ops insights, TSG writing) and the debugging agent follows incident-debugging; a profile's own skills add to or replace them, and unknown skills are refused before anything runs.

Before a plan runs it is checked against what exists now: connected peers, the folders they share with you with their checks, access and worktrees, squads, knowledge topics and skills. A plan with errors is refused with every reason, in the terminal and the web UI, and the web UI checks plans as you type.
live: a plan with errors was refused before anything ran

claims.claim: A profile signs in to GitHub with a GitHub CLI account. Linking a repository clones it with that account (the token never reaches a command line or the clone's config) into a folder outside the profiles, shared with a worktree per task; the clone syncs, task branches are listed and pushed (only p2p/... ones), and pull requests open with the profile's account. Linking needs a sign-in.
live: linked a GitHub repository with the profile's GitHub sign-in

claims.claim: The Claude/Codex bridge passes task fields, runs requests concurrently, and surfaces provider errors and bridge exits.
The command line definition is valid (no conflicting flags or subcommands).
